summary: A fast, loud party game where hidden roles and dice-based dueling create chaotic accusations at the table; it plays in about 15 minutes but scales awkwardly since eliminated players just sit out. It leans heavily on Yahtzee-style dice mechanics rather than the hand-management of the original card game, trading strategic depth for speed and noise.
praised: Very quick to teach and play
Captures the social deduction/bluffing fun of the original Bang! with less setup
Great for large groups and non-gamers
criticised: Player elimination leaves people out for the rest of the game
Can feel repetitive over multiple plays
Less depth than the original Bang! card game

interaction.kind: open conflict and accusation via bluffing

scoring.why: The game ends the moment one team's hidden win condition is met (Sheriff's side kills all outlaws, outlaws kill the Sheriff, or a renegade survives alone), not by tallying points.
